entries.title: Advice for Newlyweds
entries.moral: Moral: A happy marriage rests not on comparison or the pursuit of perfection, but on open communication, mutual respect, and care for each other’s personal boundaries.

entries.title: Aging
entries.moral: Moral: Growing older brings more than a loss of strength. Experience and wisdom can also give us a broader view of life.

entries.title: Albrecht Dürer
entries.moral: Moral: Behind success there often stands an unseen sacrifice. To recognize and honor that sacrifice is one of the finest expressions of humanity.

entries.title: The Ant Carrying Water
entries.moral: Moral: Even when you cannot change the outcome, you can stand up for what is right. Being there for someone you love in a time of trouble matters in itself.

entries.title: Sinan Brought Water to Istanbul but Died in a House Without It
entries.moral: Moral: Do not place excessive trust in fame, worldly privilege, or human remembrance. True service is rendered not for personal gain, but for what one knows to be right.

entries.title: How to Face a Problem
entries.moral: Moral: If a problem can be solved, work toward a solution. If it cannot, worrying will not change it.

entries.title: Avoid These Questions
entries.moral: Moral: Some questions wound the heart. Every painful question left unasked may lift a burden from someone’s shoulders.

entries.title: Baklava
entries.moral: Moral: Mocking another person’s poverty is among the gravest wrongs. Never forget that a mother may surrender her own share—even her final bite—for her child.

entries.title: Be Sure of Your Purpose
entries.moral: Moral: Clarify the goal before beginning the work. Otherwise, you may labor for hours while directing all your strength the wrong way.

entries.title: The Bedouin and the Stolen Camel
entries.moral: Moral: Sometimes a person bears a loss quietly to protect others’ faith in human kindness. One story of betrayal can discourage countless acts of generosity.

entries.title: Being Human
entries.moral: Moral: True worth lies not in knowledge alone, but in humanity. A heart capable of respect also makes room for love and justice.

entries.title: Belling the Cat
entries.moral: Moral: Making a plan is easier than carrying it out. Even the cleverest idea is of little use unless someone can put it into practice.

entries.title: Those Who Give Love Receive Love
entries.moral: Moral: The real poison often lies in our own thoughts. When we treat others with love, hatred can fade and enemies can become friends.

entries.title: Take Care of Those You Love
entries.moral: Moral: Every extra moment with those you love is a gift. Before it is too late, give them five more minutes today.

entries.title: The Gifts of Allah
entries.moral: Moral: Every blessing from Allah carries a responsibility; we honor His gifts by using them with justice, compassion, gratitude, and faithfulness.

entries.title: The Dry Well
entries.moral: Moral: Shake off the burdens that fall on you and use them to climb higher. When you feel helpless, action and perseverance can reveal a way out.

entries.title: Eyes That Do Not See
entries.moral: Moral: True sight requires understanding as well as eyes. We can look without seeing and listen without understanding.

entries.title: At the Bookstore
entries.moral: Moral: A small act of kindness can leave a lifelong mark on the heart. Those who receive kindness often carry it forward to others.

entries.title: The Nest Builder
entries.moral: Moral: A woman’s work builds a home and holds a family together. That work deserves recognition and appreciation.

entries.title: Adversity and Blessing
entries.moral: Moral: A hardship that brings you closer to Allah is a blessing, while a blessing that draws you away from Him becomes a hardship. What matters is where it leads you, not how comfortable it makes you.

entries.title: Can a Broken Heart Love Again?
entries.moral: Moral: Even if the heart is broken, it does not stop loving. Just as one does not stop drinking water because a vessel is broken, so too does a person continue to love.

entries.title: The Four Candles
entries.moral: Moral: When faith, loyalty, and love fade, hope can rekindle them. Keep hope alive, and the others can return.

entries.title: The Chief Accountant and the CEO
entries.moral: Moral: Investing in people is not a waste. Saving a little on their development today can lead to a much greater loss tomorrow.

entries.title: The Church Bell
entries.moral: Moral: When justice dies, something greater than the king dies. Stand by the truth so that injustice does not go unpunished.

entries.title: Communication
entries.moral: Moral: Older people offer the wisdom of experience, while children remind us of innocence. Every stage of life has something to teach us.

entries.title: Compassion
entries.moral: Moral: Compassion gives humanity its meaning. It means more than sharing someone’s tears; it means looking for a way to ease their suffering.

entries.title: A Compliment
entries.moral: Moral: A single kind word can change how a person sees themselves—and sometimes how they see the entire world. Happiness is not found in outward possessions, but within us and in the sincere attention we offer one another.

entries.title: The Credit Ledger
entries.moral: Moral: Kindness given quietly has a special worth. Relieving someone’s debt and keeping an orphan from hunger reveal a truly generous heart.

entries.title: The One Left Behind
entries.moral: Moral: The person left behind carries both love and longing. Separation can make the depth of that love painfully clear.

entries.title: The Dervish’s Appearance
entries.moral: Moral: A person who cultivates the inner life does not judge worth by outward appearance. What truly makes a person beautiful is not clothing, but a pure heart and a luminous spirit.

entries.title: The Dervish’s Robe
entries.moral: Moral: The appearance of holiness does not make a person righteous. Judge people by their actions, not their clothing; a robe alone does not make a dervish.

entries.title: The Dervish’s Long Spoons
entries.moral: Moral: Those who think only of themselves may remain hungry at life’s table. Those who care for others are nourished in return. Giving is its own reward.

entries.title: The Diderot Effect
entries.moral: Moral: Buying something new can make us feel compelled to replace everything around it. This is known as the Diderot effect. Desire has no natural stopping point; it is better to own modest possessions than to be ruled by luxurious ones.

entries.title: A Different Path
entries.moral: Moral: The path everyone follows is not always the best one. Sometimes those who step beyond habit and search for a new route reach their destination more quickly and easily.

entries.title: Discussion and Conflict
entries.moral: Moral: Conflict asks who is right; discussion asks what is right. If you want the truth, discuss — do not quarrel.

entries.title: Never Regret a Day
entries.moral: Moral: Every day offers something: happiness, experience, a lesson, or a memory. Each has its place in your life.

entries.title: Be Mindful of What You Say
entries.moral: Moral: Be careful not to deepen another person’s sense of loss. They need understanding, not reminders of what they lack.

entries.title: Do Not Let Your Hearts Drift Apart
entries.moral: Moral: Shouting reflects the distance between hearts. Even in an argument, choose words that leave a way back to each other.

entries.title: Do You Have Enough Money?
entries.moral: Moral: Show your parents that you value them through practical care. No one and nothing can replace them.

entries.title: At the Doctor’s Office
entries.moral: Moral: Judgment based only on emotion and assumption can lead us to the wrong decision. Asking about the situation before helping is itself part of compassion.

entries.title: The Donkey’s Law
entries.moral: Moral: A senseless law survives not only through a ruler’s power, but through the silence of those who obey it. An order is not necessarily wise. Do not be afraid to question it; nonsense left unchallenged can become an accepted rule.

entries.title: Neither Gossip nor Dust
entries.moral: Moral: Protect both your reputation and your dignity. Do not give people reason to gossip about you, and do not allow anyone to treat you without respect.

entries.title: Speak Kindly or Remain Silent
entries.moral: Moral: Words have value when we use them thoughtfully and for good. If you have nothing worthwhile to say, silence may be the wiser choice.

entries.title: Tomorrow Is Another Chance
entries.moral: Moral: Every day is a new page. You can't change yesterday, but how you write today is in your hands.

entries.title: The Sherbet of Martyrdom
entries.moral: Moral: An expression can carry a history of sacrifice. The words we use preserve memories of the past.

entries.title: Early Marriage
entries.moral: Moral: A teacher’s care can change a girl’s future. Early marriage can rob children of their education; we must not turn a blind eye to it.

entries.title: Eating Moderately and Living Honestly
entries.moral: Moral: Eat in moderation and act with integrity, so that you need neither a doctor nor a judge.

entries.title: Training or Nature?
entries.moral: Moral: Training may shape behavior, but an opportunity can reveal the nature beneath it. Learning matters, but character matters too.

entries.title: The Elephant and the Rope
entries.moral: Moral: Often we are held back by beliefs formed through past failures. To become free, we must also overcome the fear of what others might say.

entries.title: Everyone Has Work to Do
entries.moral: Moral: It is a very painful feeling to live knowing you are regarded as unreliable and untrustworthy.

entries.title: Everyone Is Equal Here
entries.moral: Moral: Treat a person the same because they are human, not because of their rank. Society is changed by those who choose what is right in small moments.

entries.title: It Is in Our Hands
entries.moral: Moral: Good and evil begin with choices. What shapes our lives is not simply how clever we are, but what we choose to do.

entries.title: How We Express Sorrow
entries.moral: Moral: People carry their problems in different ways: some talk, some write, some keep quiet and smile. The deepest problems are often hidden in the deepest silence.

entries.title: Words to Avoid
entries.moral: Moral: Words can hurt the person we love the most. In the family, we should use the language of respect and requests, not orders and insults.

entries.title: Confidence Is Half the Battle
entries.moral: Moral: Confidence can bring hidden abilities to life. High expectations may be the first step toward strong results.

entries.title: The King’s Missing Teeth
entries.moral: Moral: The same truth can be spoken harshly or with tact. Words can wound or heal; wisdom lies in knowing how to speak them.

entries.title: Father and Son
entries.moral: Moral: Don't hide your love, show it. Sometimes a timely step can prevent years of resentment.

entries.title: A Father’s Footsteps
entries.moral: Moral: The most powerful form of guidance is personal example. Children often imitate not what adults say, but the steps they take.

entries.title: A Festive Gift
entries.moral: Moral: The most precious gift is measured not by money, but by kindness and attention. What makes a celebration meaningful is sometimes not what you receive, but what you give.

entries.title: At the Fish Shop
entries.moral: Moral: Do not wait for great means before doing good; kindness depends not on wealth, but on a generous heart. A person rich in spirit finds a way to help even while possessing little.

entries.title: The Flower of Honesty
entries.moral: Moral: Honesty is more valuable than any outward display. Truthfulness and a clear conscience reveal a person’s worth.

entries.title: A Fly in a China Shop
entries.moral: Moral: A small lie whispered into an ignorant ear can cause enormous destruction. Knowledge, critical thinking, and strong moral values are our best protection against it.

entries.title: Life After Sixty
entries.moral: Moral: After years of caring for others, allow yourself to enjoy life too. Your happiness can brighten the lives of those around you.

entries.title: Ill-Gotten Money
entries.moral: Moral: Money taken dishonestly brings no true benefit and may cost far more than it seems to offer. Leave what is not rightfully yours.

entries.title: The Former Minister’s Cup
entries.moral: Moral: The respect shown to you is often for your position, not for yourself. Therefore, do not brag about your position — your true value will be seen when you leave.

entries.title: The Fortieth Day
entries.moral: Moral: Customs can hold generations of love and blessings. A baby’s gifts express hopes for an entire lifetime.

entries.title: Friend of Allah
entries.moral: Moral: Sometimes kindness does not descend from heaven by itself; it reaches us through good people. Perhaps you can be the answer to someone’s prayer.

entries.title: Friendship and Love
entries.moral: Moral: Let quarrels, anger, and hatred pass. Give friendship and love a lasting home in the heart.

entries.title: The Friendship of Horses
entries.moral: Moral: The Lord does not abandon us in difficult times. Help often reaches us through other people, and sometimes we are called to be that help.

entries.title: A Wise Father’s Advice to His Son
entries.moral: Moral: Wisdom is the source of happiness, and strength is the servant of wisdom. He who listens to advice will be exalted; but he who thinks he knows everything will perish.

entries.title: An Istanbul Woman Remembers
entries.moral: Moral: Don’t judge by appearance; behind every behavior there may be a truth that you don’t know. Our freedom is owed to the sacrifice of the selfless.

entries.title: The Garden and the Gardener
entries.moral: Moral: Recognize both your own efforts and the help you receive. No one grows entirely alone or entirely through the work of others.

entries.title: A Generous Man
entries.moral: Moral: Those who do good should not consider themselves the true owners of what they give. They are only instruments; the true Giver is Allah.

entries.title: A Glass of Milk
entries.moral: Moral: A selfless act of kindness is never lost. It is entered into an unseen account and may return to us one day—often when we least expect it.

entries.title: Come Again Soon
entries.moral: Moral: A subtle gesture can convey great kindness. The value given to a person is often seen in small moments.

entries.title: The Pleasure of Allah
entries.moral: Moral: Bringing joy to others draws us closer to Allah, while breaking someone’s heart leads us away from Him.

entries.title: The Goose to Be Plucked
entries.moral: Moral: A wise word is revealed to those who understand it. Not everyone understands what they hear — some answers a person must find for themselves.

entries.title: Gossip
entries.moral: Moral: A word that is spread is like a feather thrown to the wind - it cannot be collected again. Therefore, stay away from gossip.

entries.title: Grandfather and Grandson at the Market
entries.moral: Moral: Being able to control yourself in a tense moment is a sign of true strength. Keeping calm sometimes means mastering yourself, not others.

entries.title: The Little Shop and the Supermarket
entries.moral: Moral: A person who lives by the question “Whom did I help?” rather than “What did I gain?” is different. The one who gives without expecting anything in return is actually the one who gains the most.

entries.title: The Hajj Pilgrimage
entries.moral: Moral: The deepest struggle is not against an enemy outside us, but against our own uncontrolled desires. True spiritual worth is not found in outward symbols; it begins within.

entries.title: A Handful of Roasted Chickpeas
entries.moral: Moral: Sometimes who you ask matters more than what you ask for. When the giver’s hand is larger, the gift may be larger too.

entries.title: Hayat’s Life Story
entries.moral: Moral: Blind custom and a false idea of “honor” can destroy a woman’s life, a child’s life. Those who look away from early marriage, violence, and neglect are partners in that oppression.

entries.title: The King Would Not Give So Little
entries.moral: Moral: Great things begin in the family, in proper upbringing. A child who grows up honestly becomes an honest person tomorrow.

entries.title: Help Them Yourself, O Exalted Allah!
entries.moral: Moral: The last refuge of the helpless, the lonely, and the hopeless is the Creator. Prayer is the language of deepest need.

entries.title: Henry Ford's Choice
entries.moral: Moral: Small actions reveal character, both in how we make decisions and in how we treat people with less power than ourselves.

entries.title: At Least I Look Busy
entries.moral: Moral: Wasting time on empty work for the sake of appearances is the real loss. Looking busy does not bring real benefit.

entries.title: Hold My Hand
entries.moral: Moral: Love offers a steady hand. Do not simply wait for those you love to reach for you; reach out and hold on to them.

entries.title: Land and Homeland
entries.moral: Moral: Sacrifice gives a homeland its profound meaning. It is more than a place; it is land held sacred by those who have suffered for it.

entries.title: Honey or Dry Bread?
entries.moral: Moral: Your companions can lift you up or lead you astray. Plain bread shared with a wise person is worth more than honey shared with a fool.

entries.title: Fresh Bread
entries.moral: Moral: A child’s sincere prayer and a few generous hearts can transform a family’s day. Where people are willing to share, no one need go hungry.

entries.title: Letting Go of Troubling Thoughts
entries.moral: Moral: You yourself hold the thoughts that oppress you; it is in your hands to let them go. Change your perspective, and your burden will lighten.

entries.title: Refusing an Insult
entries.moral: Moral: You need not take another person’s malice into your heart. Meet an insult with composure rather than more hostility.

entries.title: Keeping the Right Distance
entries.moral: Moral: Relationships need balance. Stay close enough to share warmth, but leave enough space to avoid being hurt.

entries.title: A Human Being Emerged
entries.moral: Moral: When love, labor, conscience, loyalty, and justice come together, a true human being is formed. Humanity is the union of these values.

entries.title: Humanity
entries.moral: Moral: A profession tells us what someone does; kindness shows who they are. One act of compassion can inspire generations.

entries.title: The Hunter's Tale
entries.moral: Moral: The storyteller decides whose courage is remembered. If you cannot tell your own story, others will tell it for you.

entries.title: What I Know Now
entries.moral: Moral: True maturity is not about changing others, but about knowing who to let into your life and who to stay away from.

entries.title: I’m Tired, Mom
entries.moral: Moral: A mother’s lap can be our safest refuge. Remember that she, too, may long for someone to comfort her.

entries.title: Waiting for the Teeth
entries.moral: Moral: No one should be left in need of the one they love. May Allah not leave anyone helpless, even in their own family.

entries.title: A Little Inner Housekeeping
entries.moral: Moral: True cleanliness is in the heart: throwing away disappointment, fear, and resentment and planting love, forgiveness, and hope in their place. The one who cleans his inner world finds peace.

entries.title: I Kiss Your Eyes
entries.moral: Moral: Offer tenderness where longing has left its mark. Love recognizes what another person has endured.

entries.title: I Love You
entries.moral: Moral: Affection may go unrecognized until it is too late. Appreciate the love in your life while there is still time.

entries.title: I Want a Friend
entries.moral: Moral: A loyal friend is a greater treasure than any possession. Friendship can keep our memory alive after we are gone.

entries.title: I Would Not Trade It for Anything
entries.moral: Moral: On a beautiful, sunny day there is no place for strife, oppression, or lies. In the light, injustice, fear, and hunger cannot live.

entries.title: The Idle Devil
entries.moral: Moral: People oppress each other so much that the devil has no work to do. Most evil comes not from outside, but from within us.

entries.title: If Fate Allows
entries.moral: Moral: Do not let distance grow between you and those you care about. Instead of leaving a meeting to fate, make time for one another.

entries.title: The World Will Not Fall Apart
entries.moral: Moral: Trust is built by keeping commitments. What takes years to earn can be lost in a moment of carelessness.

entries.title: When One Door Closes
entries.moral: Moral: A closed door can lead to a better path. Losing one opportunity sometimes creates room for another.

entries.title: A Good Companion Lightens the Journey
entries.moral: Moral: It's not the road that tires you or lightens your load, but the person next to you. A true companion makes even the hardest task easier.

entries.title: Wasted Effort
entries.moral: Moral: Choosing your company helps shape your life. Do not waste it arguing with people unwilling to learn or trusting those who are insincere.

entries.title: It Won’t Go to Waste
entries.moral: Moral: Kindness, words, and deeds from the heart never vanish; they light others’ way and brighten your life.

entries.title: The Judge of Frankfurt
entries.moral: Moral: Greed traps a person. The stingy person who denies the truth eventually becomes a victim of his own lies; justice is on the side of the righteous.

entries.title: Know Your Friend
entries.moral: Moral: A friend is known in trouble, in hardship, and in the test of advantage. Everyone is a friend in good times; a true friend is revealed in adversity.

entries.title: A Lawful Morsel
entries.moral: Moral: A child’s moral formation begins with the food placed on the family table. Lawful earnings and honest nourishment help lay the foundation of sound character.

entries.title: The Lecturer and the Stablehand
entries.moral: Moral: Good speaking is not measured by length. What matters is whether your listener can understand and absorb what you say.

entries.title: May the Prayer You Need Find You
entries.moral: Moral: When you help those in need and show tenderness to the vulnerable, you become worthy of others’ prayers. The kindness you offer today may return to you when you need it most.

entries.title: Life Is Short
entries.moral: Moral: Give your time to relationships that bring love and joy into your life.

entries.title: A Life Lesson
entries.moral: Moral: Sometimes the greatest harm comes from those who resemble us while concealing different intentions. Recognizing hypocrisy in time is the first step toward protecting oneself.

entries.title: The Door of the Heart
entries.moral: Moral: The door of the heart opens only from the inside. Love and goodness do not force their way in - you must let them in yourself.

entries.title: The Lion's Track
entries.moral: Moral: A person is known not by his pretensions, but by his behavior in the moment of trial. Many people "look for a lion" from afar, but when they come face to face, most of them retreat.

entries.title: The Liver in Language
entries.moral: Moral: Language does not arise by chance; behind every word there is a history, a belief. Our words are the memory of our past.

entries.title: Living in the Past
entries.moral: Moral: You cannot undo the past. Turn toward the future and give yourself a chance to move forward.

entries.title: Loving from Afar
entries.moral: Moral: Fear of losing someone can keep us from expressing our feelings. Yet love left unspoken carries its own loss.

entries.title: A Magnificent Lesson
entries.moral: Moral: In education, personal example is stronger than any lecture. A responsible parent may even set aside personal pride to help a child find the right path.

entries.title: A Mature Person
entries.moral: Moral: Maturity is the ability to step away from harmful relationships and protect one’s inner peace. Knowing whom—and what—to keep at a distance is also a form of wisdom.

entries.title: May You Always Have Reason to Smile
entries.moral: Moral: Warmth draws people to us. A smile costs nothing, yet can make all the difference.

entries.title: A Meaningless Question
entries.moral: Moral: An answer to a meaningless question cannot lead to truth. A well-formed question is already half the answer.

entries.title: Meddling in Other People’s Lives
entries.moral: Moral: Unwanted advice can become a burden. Calling interference “kindness” does not prevent it from doing harm.

entries.title: Mercedes
entries.moral: Moral: A name given with love, a work done with love can change the world. A father's love immortalized a name.

entries.title: Mihrimah Sultan and Architect Sinan
entries.moral: Moral: Being united with the one you love is not always granted. Sometimes a person turns that love into a work that outlives the one who felt it.

entries.title: Teach Children Not to Mock
entries.moral: Moral: Teach children early that differences are no excuse for ridicule. Every person deserves dignity.

entries.title: A More Effective Way
entries.moral: Moral: Hard work is valuable, but unexamined effort can be wasteful. Sometimes a short pause to sharpen the tool makes all the work that follows faster and easier.

entries.title: The Finest Gifts
entries.moral: Moral: Every relationship has its own best gift: honor for a father, respect for a mother, loyalty to a friend, service to humanity.

entries.title: The Most Beautiful Places
entries.moral: Moral: Our dearest place is not always somewhere on a map. It may be in a loved one’s heart.

entries.title: The Finest Blessing
entries.moral: Moral: Being listened to with care is a form of being loved.

entries.title: Mother and Son
entries.moral: Moral: The child who once feared being left may one day leave a parent with the same fear. Caring for parents means attending to their need for love as well as their physical needs.

entries.title: The Mother-of-Pearl Flower
entries.moral: Moral: Love is sometimes expressed through years of quiet care. Recognize that care, and remember to speak gently to those you love.

entries.title: The Advice Fakir Baykurt Never Forgot
entries.moral: Moral: Don't kill the "lion" inside a child — his self-confidence — by beating him. True education is not given with fear, but with patience and love.

entries.title: A Mother’s Love
entries.moral: Moral: A mother’s love is unconditional and irreplaceable. Make time for those you love today, because time is the most precious thing we can never recover.

entries.title: The Mullah and the Scholar
entries.moral: Moral: The same sign is read differently in each person’s world. We often see the other in the mirror of our own thoughts.

entries.title: My Alif Has Been Dotted
entries.moral: Moral: A single letter—or a single moment—can turn joy into sorrow. Expressions preserve the feelings and stories behind them.

entries.title: Newton’s Second Law
entries.moral: Moral: Before teaching a subject, make sure you understand it yourself. Repetition alone cannot replace clarity.

entries.title: Sane in a World Gone Mad
entries.moral: Moral: The crowd may condemn you for knowing the truth. Protect your mind, but don't tire yourself out by trying to prove your worth to the public every moment.

entries.title: The Same Complaint
entries.moral: Moral: Repetition alone changes nothing. Give your energy to finding a way forward.

entries.title: Choose Your Confidants Carefully
entries.moral: Moral: Trust your pain to people who will treat it with care.

entries.title: Staying on the Right Path
entries.moral: Moral: A person who gives full attention to what is right and remembers that Allah sees his actions is far less likely to lose his way.

entries.title: Nothing Is Ever Truly Lost
entries.moral: Moral: Learn from failure, and the experience has not been wasted.

entries.title: O Allah, Give First to the Mountains and Stones
entries.moral: Moral: True generosity means thinking of others before oneself. This prayer carries within it an entire people’s tradition of sharing.

entries.title: O Allah, Grant Relief from Our Troubles
entries.moral: Moral: When we recognize our helplessness and pray sincerely, the heart finds peace. Prayer is the language of hope and trust in Allah.

entries.title: Knowing What You Know
entries.moral: Moral: Teach the one who yearns to learn, awaken the one who is heedless, stay away from the ignorant who thinks he knows everything, and follow the one who really knows.

entries.title: Only My Mother’s Tears
entries.moral: Moral: A mother’s love is cherished for its sincerity and its willingness to ask nothing in return.

entries.title: An Organization Without an Action Plan
entries.moral: Moral: A goal provides direction; a plan defines the path toward it. An organization may advance by chance without a plan, but lasting success requires deliberate and consistent action.

entries.title: Other People's Opinions
entries.moral: Moral: When we surrender our own voice and understanding, other people’s ideas take their place. Preserve the values and roots that help you remain yourself.

entries.title: When Strengths Become Weaknesses
entries.moral: Moral: What gives us pride can also become a weakness. Recognize the risks that accompany your gifts.

entries.title: A Pair of Boots
entries.moral: Moral: The finest victory is to value another person’s joy above one’s own. True compassion is revealed in the willingness to surrender an opportunity for someone else.

entries.title: The Pawn and the King
entries.moral: Moral: Do not underestimate the humble or place too much faith in rank. A pawn can rise, and a king can fall.

entries.title: Rent for the Water
entries.moral: Moral: Dishonesty can trap the person who practices it. Fair judgment considers both sides of a claim.

entries.title: People Who Need You
entries.moral: Moral: Instead of resenting those who seek you only when they need something, think that they come because they trust you — and your heart will be at ease.

entries.title: Permission or Apology
entries.moral: Moral: When an action is low risk, reversible, and clearly useful, excessive approval processes can stifle initiative. Responsible action sometimes achieves more than endless waiting.

entries.title: The Strength of Truth
entries.moral: Moral: Truth is unbending and unyielding. Even though time passes and power changes, in the end, the righteous one stands firm.

entries.title: Gratitude at the Kitchen Sink
entries.moral: Moral: Everyday chores can remind us of everyday blessings. Gratitude begins with noticing them.

entries.title: The Price of a Miracle
entries.moral: Moral: Faith is a powerful force. Sometimes, when a child’s pure faith meets the kindness of a human being, a miracle is born.

entries.title: What Water Teaches Us
entries.moral: Moral: Human connection keeps the heart alive, just as movement keeps water fresh.

entries.title: Puppies for Sale
entries.moral: Moral: Every living thing needs a friend who will understand and support it. The one who is different is just as valuable as the others; we need to give him a chance.

entries.title: The Purple Chepken
entries.moral: Moral: Violence against women is unacceptable. When society considers it a duty of conscience to protect women, there is no room for oppression.

entries.title: Parenting
entries.moral: Moral: A child is educated not with fear, but with love. It is not a teacher or an outsider who educates a child—it is a loving parent.

entries.title: Ramadan Prayer
entries.moral: Moral: Sincere prayer fills the heart with hope and mercy. The wish for blessings, healing, and forgiveness brings a person closer to the Creator.

entries.title: The Red Dress
entries.moral: Moral: Loving others should not mean abandoning your own life. Leave room for your needs and hopes too.

entries.title: The Road Beyond the Cotton Fields
entries.moral: Moral: A teacher not only showed the way to children, but also created new paths for them. For a person who can dream, the world no longer consists of just one path.

entries.title: The Rose
entries.moral: Moral: Love and care need balance. Too much control can harm, just as neglect can; attentive care helps life flourish.

entries.title: The Seed That Grew
entries.moral: Moral: Words either build or destroy. It is possible to elevate or destroy someone with a single word—every seed watered with love will germinate.

entries.title: Meat for the Feast
entries.moral: Moral: A celebration is complete only when others can share in it. In times of abundance, remember the neighbors who are going without.

entries.title: Speak What You Know
entries.moral: Moral: Speak honestly, listen thoughtfully, and know when to be silent. See people as they are, without contempt or flattery.

entries.title: The Right Words at the Right Time
entries.moral: Moral: Thoughtful words spare regret. The right words at the right moment are precious.

entries.title: The Scarf Seller
entries.moral: Moral: Sometimes the most helpless person shows the greatest generosity. The pure heart of a child turns material poverty into wealth.

entries.title: Searching in the Wrong Place
entries.moral: Moral: Do not expect everyone to offer what they do not possess. See people clearly, rather than through your hopes for them.

entries.title: The Secret of a Long and Happy Life
entries.moral: Moral: Eat little, walk a lot, laugh a lot, love endlessly. The secret to a long and happy life lies in simplicity and love.

entries.title: Sharing Fairly
entries.moral: Moral: Humanity is created when joy, bread, and love are shared. If one side laughs and the other side cries, there is no justice there.

entries.title: Call the Shepherd
entries.moral: Moral: Not every problem can be solved by force. Sometimes taking a step back and looking at it differently is the shortest way out.

entries.title: The Shepherd's Word
entries.moral: Moral: Our true wealth lies in an honest conscience and a word others can trust.

entries.title: Silence
entries.moral: Moral: Sometimes silence is the wisest response. Consider both the moment and the person asking.

entries.title: The Silent Corridor
entries.moral: Moral: When communication is unclear, even the best work can go unnoticed. When there is no consistent follow-up, even the strongest partnership can falter. In collaboration, the greatest enemy is often not failure—it is silence.

entries.title: The Skins of the Lambs
entries.moral: Moral: It is more just to take the unjust profit of the wealthy than to rob the poor. The burden should be placed on the strong, not the poor.

entries.title: The Sound of the Doorbell
entries.moral: Moral: For some people, one ring of the doorbell, one greeting, is worth the whole world. Let's not forget to knock on the door of the lonely.

entries.title: The Saplings That Bore Gold
entries.moral: Moral: A person does not live only for himself. We ate what those who came before us planted; we must plant for those who come after us.

entries.title: Making Time
entries.moral: Moral: Time is the only wealth that never comes back. Appreciate the person who willingly spends it for you.

entries.title: Spend time with people
entries.moral: Moral: Technology provides convenience, but it does not replace life. The real value is in live communication, in the warmth between people.

entries.title: Spinach
entries.moral: Moral: We often understand a mother's sacrifice in the face of impossibility years later. Love is sometimes hidden in a plate of simple food.

entries.title: Stoning the Devil
entries.moral: Moral: The real struggle is not only against evil outside us, but against the uncontrolled desires within. Purifying oneself is harder than condemning others, but far more valuable.

entries.title: Strength and Pain
entries.moral: Moral: In suffering, we may pray for greater strength or a lighter burden.

entries.title: The Strongest Shield
entries.moral: Moral: Healthy distance can protect your peace. You need not remain close to everything or everyone that hurts you.

entries.title: Do You Remember Me?
entries.moral: Moral: To protect a person’s dignity without shaming them — by closing your eyes — is true teaching. A person whose dignity is kept learns from the mistake and rises.

entries.title: Lying
entries.moral: Moral: Sometimes the kind words you tell yourself — “you can do it” — become the force that drives you forward. A person is as strong as he believes in himself.

entries.title: Not Mine to Give
entries.moral: Moral: Impartiality can demand a terrible personal sacrifice. In this story, a father refuses to claim for his son what has been reserved for others.

entries.title: Think, Speak, Act Positively
entries.moral: Moral: Thoughts shape words, words shape actions, and repeated actions become habits and values. A change in outlook can begin a change in life.

entries.title: This Boat Is Empty Too
entries.moral: Moral: If a person wants to maintain his peace, he should not look for evil intentions behind every incident. Sometimes what worries us is just a coincidence; it is our choice whether to magnify it and turn it into anger.

entries.title: Choose Your Friends Wisely
entries.moral: Moral: Arrogance, conceit, and cowardice can make friendship painful. Look for kindness, humility, and loyalty.

entries.title: The Three Best Things
entries.moral: Moral: The best food is found in hunger, the best sleep after hard work, and the best home is found in hearts. Happiness is not in opportunity, but in perspective.

entries.title: Three Things a City Needs
entries.moral: Moral: A city must care for the inner life of its people as well as their physical surroundings.

entries.title: Three Scenes
entries.moral: Moral: The three scenes warn against boasting of good deeds and growing accustomed to wrongdoing, while honoring the value of wise spiritual guidance.

entries.title: Three Questions
entries.moral: Moral: Position is never permanent. Remember that circumstances can change, and remain humble.

entries.title: The Three Statues
entries.moral: Moral: The most valuable person is the one who can keep what he hears as a secret in his heart and only speaks when it is appropriate. Keeping your word is also a form of wisdom.

entries.title: Loneliness
entries.moral: Moral: The biggest pain is to feel lonely even among people. Seeing the loneliness of someone next to you is true sensitivity.

entries.title: Keeping a Cool Head
entries.moral: Moral: The best decision is made with a calm mind, not in a panic. Cool-headedness can turn even a difficult situation into a good one.

entries.title: Fasting
entries.moral: Moral: If a person abstains from food and does not abstain from lying, backbiting, insulting, and evil deeds, he is not fully experiencing the spiritual spirit of fasting.

entries.title: Sharing and Division
entries.moral: Moral: Sharing strengthens us; division weakens us. Unity needs care and a shared sense of purpose.

entries.title: Believe in Yourself
entries.moral: Moral: Value yourself, do not lose hope, protect your dignity. Self-confidence is a person's strongest support.

entries.title: Dreaming
entries.moral: Moral: Trust that the dreams in your heart have meaning, and do not lose hope.

entries.title: Forgiveness
entries.moral: Moral: Forgiving is not about justifying the other person - it is about freeing yourself from the prison of hatred and resentment. Forgive and be relieved, but do not forget the lesson.

entries.title: Knowing When to Walk Away
entries.moral: Moral: Stepping back from people who disregard your values can be an act of self-respect.

entries.title: Meeting and Knowing
entries.moral: Moral: First impressions do not always survive familiarity. Knowing someone better can bring disappointment.

entries.title: Language
entries.moral: Moral: If the language is not protected, it will wither and disappear like a flower that is not watered. Keeping your mother tongue alive means using it lovingly every day.

entries.title: True Love
entries.moral: Moral: Only time knows the worth of true love. Time keeps sincere love alive and lets the false fade into forgetfulness.

entries.title: Try Another Way of Thinking
entries.moral: Moral: Changing your mindset is the first step to changing your life. Saying “I can't” closes the door, saying “I can learn” opens up new possibilities. Failure is not the end, it is an opportunity for growth.

entries.title: Turning Hardship into Opportunity
entries.moral: Moral: A difficulty can become a chance to learn or grow. How we respond helps shape what comes of it.

entries.title: What the Tortoise Forgot
entries.moral: Moral: You can calculate every difficulty in life, but not people with bad intentions. May Allah not let you face those who prevent you from moving forward, but those who support you.

entries.title: Two Cups of Water
entries.moral: Moral: The value of riches depends on what we need. In a desert, water can be worth more than a treasury.

entries.title: The Two Donkeys
entries.moral: Moral: An attempt to make someone else look foolish can expose your own foolishness instead.

entries.title: The Value of Your Family
entries.moral: Moral: The greatest need of children is the attention, love, and time spent with them by their parents.

entries.title: We Are Rich
entries.moral: Moral: True wealth is not in the treasury, but in the people’s well-being. A leader’s greatness lies not in the post, but in the meaning given to that post.

entries.title: Pull Out the Roots
entries.moral: Moral: Deal with the roots of a problem or a bad habit. Clearing away only what shows above the surface does not stop it from returning.

entries.title: The Weight of Butter
entries.moral: Moral: As you treat others, you often receive the same measure in return. The bread you give comes back to you as butter.

entries.title: Welcome Home
entries.moral: Moral: A lifetime of waiting bears witness to love and loss. Remember both those who died for their homeland and the families who waited for them.

entries.title: An Eraser for Marriage
entries.moral: Moral: Marriage is the art of forgiveness. For love and respect to continue, both parties must be able to "erase" each other's flaws.

entries.title: What Changed After Sixty
entries.moral: Moral: Age teaches a person the greatest wisdom: peace is better than perfection, and understanding is better than being right.

entries.title: What Is It to Me?
entries.moral: Moral: A society weakens when people see injustice and say, “What is it to me?” Indifference allows oppression to grow.

entries.title: What Is a Word?
entries.moral: Moral: A word can be both a wounding thorn and a precious pearl. What makes the difference is how you use it.

entries.title: What Is Loyalty?
entries.moral: Moral: Loyalty means staying present in hard times. It is shown through actions, not declarations.

entries.title: Before It Is Too Late
entries.moral: Moral: Expressing love, forgiving, and apologizing on time is beautiful. Life is short - let us not postpone the affairs of the heart.

entries.title: What Matters Most
entries.moral: Moral: Fill the jar of life with the most valuable things first—family, love, and health. If you get caught up in the little things, there will be no room for the important things.

entries.title: What Life Teaches Us
entries.moral: Moral: Every encounter can teach us something—either how to behave or how not to.

entries.title: What Women Have Endured
entries.moral: Moral: There can be no peace or love where a woman is not valued. It is the duty of society to see her work and heart.

entries.title: Where Does Misfortune Begin?
entries.moral: Moral: The root of what happens to us can often be found in our own actions. Check your eyes, your tongue, your hands, and your steps.

entries.title: Where Does This Road Go?
entries.moral: Moral: The road stays where it is. The important thing is knowing where you want to go.

entries.title: Who Handles Honey Licks His Finger
entries.moral: Moral: Even a small share in a job usually brings some gain from it.

entries.title: Why Am I Poor?
entries.moral: Moral: There is always something to give: a smile, a kind word, a compassionate look, a helping hand. A person is as rich as they share.

entries.title: Why Wait for the End of the World?
entries.moral: Moral: Make time now to love, forgive, and appreciate life.

entries.title: Why Choose Injustice?
entries.moral: Moral: When love, peace, friendship, and justice are possible, we are responsible for choosing them.

entries.title: Why Do We Shout?
entries.moral: Moral: Screaming is the sound of hearts drifting apart. A whisper is enough in love — don't increase the distance between you.

entries.title: A Windmill Turning in Still Air
entries.moral: Moral: Results have causes, even when we cannot see them. Look beyond the obvious for the forces at work.

entries.title: The Strength of a Generous People
entries.moral: Moral: A people’s strength rests in honesty and generosity. Winning hearts is a greater victory than winning territory.

entries.title: The Woman and the Mirror
entries.moral: Moral: We cannot control every change, but our outlook can help us meet it with good humor.

entries.title: The Woman Whose House Was Robbed
entries.moral: Moral: People’s sense of security grows from trust in those responsible for protecting them. When people know their ruler is keeping watch, they can sleep peacefully in their own homes.

entries.title: Words and Silence
entries.moral: Moral: Not every word blooms; some hurt like thorns. Silence is wiser than words that will not bring good.

entries.title: Yellow and Red Flowers
entries.moral: Moral: A small, thoughtful signal can express care and invite respect. Consideration does not need a raised voice.

entries.title: Would You Trust His Rope?
entries.moral: Moral: A person gains or loses trust in his name by the quality of his work. Once trust is shaken, it is very difficult to restore it.

entries.title: Your True Friends
entries.moral: Moral: A true friend is one who is there for you when you are in trouble. It is not the many acquaintances that are valuable, but the few friends who stand the test.

entries.title: Work with Your Hands and Trust in Allah
entries.moral: Moral: A person who looks at the share of the needy despite having the strength is not trusting in Allah - he is simply covering up his laziness with faith.
